query: Who wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude?
answer: The Colombian writer Gabriel García Márquez wrote *One Hundred Years of Solitude* (*Cien años de soledad*). It first came out in Argentina in May 1967, and Gregory Rabassa's English translation followed in 1970 [1]. The novel follows several generations of the Buendía family in the fictional town of Macondo [1]. When García Márquez won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982, the award citation singled this book out. He died in 2014 [1][2].
